profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Quant Research workstream and the Data Platform workstream at a corporate and investment bank, held eight business days before an internal model review for a history-augmented collaborative filtering recommender used to prioritize dealer responses to G10 bond RFQs. The model relies on recent client and instrument interaction histories, and the two workstreams need to align on the final training extract, temporal feature export, review-ready model outputs, and where the handoff will be published. The agenda is to confirm what 'data as of March 31st' means for the final run, ensure the export contains the model's 'latest history' fields, align on what will be delivered as the 'model outputs' for review consumers, and confirm publication into the project's workspace. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on timing, interfaces, and deliverables for the upcoming handoff, while several second-order assumptions remain silently misaligned.

members.name: Elena Moreau
members.expertise: Recommender systems, temporal modeling, offline evaluation for financial ML
members.background: Elena leads a quant research team building ranking models for sales and trading workflows; she previously worked on sequence models for electronic trading data and now owns the research package for the internal model review of the RFQ recommender.
members.private_state: She needs a stable, familiar extract fast so her team can finish experiments, generate review materials, and avoid any late-cycle reruns caused by schema or population drift.
hidden_assumptions: "Data as of March 31st" naturally refers to an event-time snapshot cut at end of day on March 31, matching how the research team has been prototyping.
"Latest history" means the last 20 prior interactions available before each RFQ event, because the model architecture expects fixed-length recent sequences.
"Model outputs" for the review are the ranked recommendations and summary performance tables that go into the review deck, with row-level replay artifacts only needed if someone asks later.
The "project workspace" refers to the existing research S3 workspace already used by the quant team for this project, with parquet files laid out similarly to prior extracts.

members.name: Marcus Klein
members.expertise: Market data pipelines, governed data releases, analytics delivery controls
members.background: Marcus coordinates delivery of governed datasets from trading and client activity systems into analytics environments and is responsible for lineage, auditability, and making sure research handoffs can transition into controlled implementation paths.
members.private_state: He wants the final handoff to conform to standard platform release practices so it is auditable and reusable beyond the immediate model review, and he is wary of bespoke research-only artifacts becoming the de facto official version.
hidden_assumptions: "Data as of March 31st" means the certified month-end business-date release for March, published after reconciliation in the first days of April and identified by the official release version.

"Latest history" refers to the standard trailing 30-calendar-day interaction window before each RFQ, because platform temporal exports are defined by business-time windows rather than sequence length.

"Model outputs" should include the row-level scored population, keys, and lineage needed for governance replay, because review consumers downstream will expect to inspect and reproduce the output set.
The "project workspace" is the governed delivery workspace provisioned by Data Platform for this model release, not the informal research bucket used during prototyping.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to run the final package using the data 'as of March 31st'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a research event-time extract cut exactly at end of day March 31, so every RFQ and prior interaction is included only if it was observable by that timestamp.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the certified March month-end business-date release, which is produced a few days later after reconciliation and may contain corrections or late-arriving records still attributed to March 31.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In the bank, both sides routinely speak in business dates rather than physical publish timestamps, so 'as of March 31st' sounds precise and institutional even though one hears an event-time cutoff and the other hears a reconciled month-end release.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the export should carry the model's 'latest history' for each RFQ.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the last 20 prior client-instrument interactions before the target RFQ, regardless of whether those interactions span a few days or several months.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means all interactions falling within the trailing 30 calendar days before the RFQ, because that is the platform's standard criterion for recent activity.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both hear 'latest history' as a natural label for temporal context and neither expects a coordination discussion to unpack whether recency is defined by fixed count or elapsed time, since each treats their own convention as obvious infrastructure detail.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on delivering the 'model outputs' for the review package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the ranked recommendation tables, top-K examples, and aggregate performance metrics used in the model review deck and supporting note.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the full row-level scored dataset plus keys, score columns, and lineage metadata so governance and implementation teams can replay exactly what was reviewed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'model outputs' is standard enough that both assume it already excludes debate: Elena hears the consumable research results, while Marcus hears the auditable machine-readable output set; because both are legitimate outputs of a model, the boundary difference stays hidden.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Marcus will publish the handoff into the 'project workspace'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the quant team's established research workspace in S3 where prior prototype extracts and notebooks already point, so her team can pick up parquet files immediately.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the governed Data Platform workspace created for the release, with controlled access, manifests, and delivery conventions tied to this model review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both know there is a single project and both organizations use the phrase 'project workspace' in status conversations, so each silently resolves the reference to the workspace they habitually use without realizing there are two live locations bearing the same practical label.

turns.inner_thought: We are eight business days out, so I need this pinned down without opening any new debates. I want the same research event-time cut at end of day March 31 that we've been prototyping on, dropped into the existing quant S3 workspace in the familiar parquet layout. If they keep the latest history exactly as the last 20 prior interactions before each RFQ, our sequence encoder will run unchanged. And for review, what matters is getting the ranked recommendations and summary performance material ready for the deck; anything heavier can wait unless someone asks.
